name: January 16, 2024 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 16, 2024
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Guldimann called the meeting to order at 5:38 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Vice Chair Suzanne Guldimann; and Commissioners Georgia Goldfarb, Alicia
  Peak, and Dane Skophammer

  ABSENT: Chair Cayley Jenner

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Kate Manisco,
  Recreation Manager; Chris Orosz, Recreation Supervisor; and Brittany Saleaumua,
  Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Chair Guldimann led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Chair
  Jenner was absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on January 12, 2024.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENT ATIO NS

  None.

ITEM2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-
  0, Chair Jenner absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the August 15, 2023 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting and the September 19, 2023
  Parks and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in December 2023.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Parks and Recreation Commission Rules of Procedures and Decorum
  Recommended Action: Adopt Parks and Recreation Commission Resolution No.
  24-01 Rules of Procedure and Decorum amending Section 4.C. Regular Meeting
  Schedule.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Vice Chair Guldimann stated Commissioners would benefit from starting the
  meeting at 6:30 PM.

MOTION  Commissioner Skophammer moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion
  to adopt Parks and Recreation Commission Resolution No. 24-01 Rules of
  Procedure and Decorum amending Section 4.C. Regular Meeting Schedule to 6:30
  PM. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Chair Jenner absent.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Parks and Recreation Commission Mid-Year Activity Report
  Recommended Action: Review and approve the Parks and Recreation Commission
  Mid-Year Activity Report covering the period of July through December 2023.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated weed
  abatement was completed in June of each year.
   Parks and Recreation Commission

  Page 3 of 5

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated that the Mid-Year Activity Report
  included work completed from July through December 2023.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
  Mid-Year Activity Report covered broad topics, such as field space, programs, and
  facility rentals.

  Commissioner Goldfarb requested to include Legacy Park outreach programming.

  Vice Chair Guldimann stated the report reflected the Commission's work and it
  was their resume.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated she wanted to inform the public on Legacy Park
  outreach and restoration programs.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Director Riesgo
  suggested revising the report from "Reviewed bi-monthly staff updates regarding
  the Legacy Park Rehabilitation Project" to, "Reviewed bi-monthly staff updates
  and provided input on outreach programming regarding the Legacy Park
  Rehabilitation Project."

  The Commission indicated agreement with Community Services Director Riesgo.

  Commissioner Peak suggested correlating the Council assignment number with the
  completed item in the Mid-Year Activity Report.

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved, and Commissioner Skophammer seconded a motion
  to approve the Parks and Recreation Commission Mid-Year Activity Report
  revising "Reviewed bi-monthly staff updates regarding the Legacy Park
  Rehabilitation Project" to state "Reviewed bi-monthly staff updates and provided
  input on outreach programming regarding the Legacy Park Rehabilitation Project."
  The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Chair Jenner absent.

  B.  Earth Friendly Management Policy Update
  Recommended Action:  Receive and file a report on the Earth Friendly
  Management Policy activities and quarterly report for July to December 2023.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the City
  provided hiking programs at Charmlee Wilderness Park. He stated the Earth
  Friendly Management Policy outreach included Legacy Park due to its central
  location and options for Pepperdine University students to volunteer.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated
  Legacy Park rehabilitation work was ongoing due to the native landscape.

  Vice Chair Guldimann stated Legacy Park required constant maintenance.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated all the parks had ongoing and regular
  maintenance schedules.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, the Recreation Supervisor Orosz provided a
  brief overview of the new Legacy Park Agents of Discovery application that
  focused on native plants, pollinators, and animals.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated based on the success of the application, the City would consider expanding
  it to Malibu Bluffs Park.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided an update on Breakfast with Santa,
  afterschool programs, the Student Art Exhibition, aquatic programs, and the Senior
  Center.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on the Permanent Skate
  Park and reminded the Commission that the meetings would start at 6:30 p.m.
  beginning with the February 20, 2024 Regular meeting.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Skophammer stated the ad hoc committee was evaluating the
  Malibu Aquatics Foundation and the Malibu Marlins Swim Club and would report
  their findings to the Commission. He stated that his daughter was enrolled in the
  Nature Detectives program at Malibu Elementary School, and his older daughter
  was playing in the youth basketball league.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
  Commission could prioritize Permanent Skate Park fundraising and would provide
  the project cost estimate.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated the Pepperdine University partnership and the
  outreach programs at Legacy Park were great.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 6:39 p.m., Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Commissioner Skophammer
  seconded a motion to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion
  carried 4-0, Vice Chair Jenner absent.

  Approved and adopted by the Parks and
  Recreation Commission of the City of
  Malibu on March 19, 2024.
